body: WarioWare: Smooth Moves is Nintendo and Intelligent Systems' Wii collection of very short games built around different ways of holding the Wii Remote. Wario and the other inhabitants of Diamond City introduce stages in which a simple instruction must be understood and performed within seconds. The controller may become an umbrella, a handle or something held against the body. Each new pose prepares the next joke and the next action, making the player's changing posture part of the spectacle as much as the images appearing on the television.

Before a microgame begins, an illustration demonstrates how to hold the Remote. The following prompt then asks for a brief movement or decision using that position. Failing costs one of the stage's lives, while a sequence of successful actions leads toward a longer boss challenge. The format leaves little time for explanation, relying on recognisable objects and readable motions. A player learns to connect the suggested pose with the immediate situation, turning a few seconds of confusion into the satisfaction of understanding what the game expects.

Completing the single-player stages opens multiplayer activities in which one Wii Remote can be shared by a group of up to twelve. Watching another person perform an unusual pose becomes part of the entertainment before the controller reaches the next player. The arrangement gives a rapid succession of small games a social rhythm beyond the screen. Smooth Moves uses the Wii's motion controls as a source of physical comedy, making the act of discovering how to hold the controller inseparable from discovering how to play the next game.
